data.content_ref: inline:The target selects city size as the single dominant cross-city modulator, but its own counterconditions expose the flaw: nocturnal UHI intensity is empirically governed by urban canyon geometry (sky view factor, building height-to-width ratio) and impervious surface fraction, not by spatial extent. Dense compact cities with deep street canyons consistently produce larger nocturnal temperature gaps than sprawling low-density cities of equal or greater area, because reduced sky view factor traps longwave radiation. The target's mechanism conflates total thermal mass with per-area energy balance, and its scaling claim fails when per-area storage is held constant.
